beige.explanation: "Beige" means "beige". To ask about a color and answer: "Hvilken farve har huset?" "Det er beige." (Which color is the house? It is beige.)

bekendt.explanation: "Bekendt" means "familiar". When you talk about a person you know only slightly, use the noun "en bekendt" (an acquaintance): "Jeg mødte en bekendt i byen" (I met an acquaintance in town). To say you know about something, use "med" (with) after it: "Jeg er bekendt med reglerne" (I am familiar with the rules).

bekvem.explanation: "Bekvem" means "convenient". When you talk about a seat or clothes that feel good, it also means "comfortable": "en bekvem stol" (a comfortable chair). It is built into "en bekvemmelighed" (a convenience).

bekymrende.explanation: "Bekymrende" means "worrying". To say the news or a sign causes worry, use "bekymrende": "Nyheden er bekymrende" (The news is worrying). To say you feel worry yourself, use the similar word "bekymret" (worried): "Jeg er bekymret" (I am worried).

belysning.explanation: "Belysning" means "lighting". It comes from the verb "at belyse" (to illuminate). When you talk about looking closely at a subject, it has another meaning: "en belysning af sagen" (a closer look at the matter).

bemærkelsesværdig.explanation: "Bemærkelsesværdig" means "remarkable". It is built from "at bemærke" (to notice) and "værdig" (worthy). To say that a fact deserves attention, say: "Det er bemærkelsesværdigt, at hun vandt" (It is remarkable that she won).

benzin.explanation: "Benzin" means "gasoline". To say you fill the car with fuel, use the verb "at tanke" (to fill up): "Jeg skal tanke benzin" (I need to fill up with gasoline).

beredvillighed.explanation: "En beredvillighed" means "a readiness", as in readiness to help. Do not mix it up with "et beredskab" (an emergency service): "Beredskabet kom hurtigt" (The emergency service came quickly).

berettiget.explanation: "Berettiget" means "justified". When you say someone has the right to receive something, it means "entitled" and takes "til" (to): "Du er berettiget til hjælp" (You are entitled to help).

beruset.explanation: "Beruset" means "intoxicated". It is the formal word, as in "en beruset bilist" (an intoxicated driver). In everyday talk, to say someone is drunk, use "fuld": "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

beskadiget.explanation: "Beskadiget" means "damaged". It comes from the verb "at beskadige" (to damage). To say a package arrived with harm, say: "Pakken er beskadiget" (The package is damaged). To say a thing no longer works at all, use the similar word "ødelagt" (broken): "Telefonen er ødelagt" (The phone is broken).

beskeden.explanation: "Beskeden" means "modest". When you talk about a small amount, it has another meaning: "en beskeden løn" (a modest salary). Do not mix it up with "en besked" (a message): "Jeg fik en besked" (I got a message).

beskidt.explanation: "Beskidt" means "dirty". To say you made something dirty, use it after "at gøre" (to make): "Jeg har gjort tøjet beskidt" (I have made the clothes dirty).

beskyttelse.explanation: "En beskyttelse" means "a protection". It comes from the verb "at beskytte" (to protect). The word begins many compounds, such as "beskyttelsesbriller" (safety goggles).

beskyttende.explanation: "Beskyttende" means "protective". It comes from the verb "at beskytte" (to protect). When you talk about a person who watches over someone, use it too: "en beskyttende far" (a protective father).

beslutsomhed.explanation: "En beslutsomhed" means "a determination". Do not mix it up with "en beslutning" (a decision): "Vi tog en beslutning" (We made a decision).

beslægtet.explanation: "Beslægtet" means "related". To ask whether two people are in the same family, say: "Er I beslægtede?" (Are you two related?). It comes from "en slægt" (a family line).

bestemt.explanation: "Bestemt" means "definitely". To stress that something is certain, put it in the sentence: "Hun kommer bestemt" (She is definitely coming). To point at one particular thing, it means "certain": "en bestemt bog" (a certain book).

bestemt form.explanation: "En bestemt form" means "a definite form". It is the version of a word that says "the". Danish puts "the" on the end of the word: "en hund" (a dog) becomes "hunden" (the dog). For a word with "et", the same happens: "et hus" (a house) becomes "huset" (the house).

bestik.explanation: "Et bestik" means "a set of cutlery". To name one piece of cutlery, say "en kniv" (a knife), "en gaffel" (a fork) or "en ske" (a spoon).

bestikkelse.explanation: "En bestikkelse" means "a bribe". It comes from the verb "at bestikke" (to bribe). To name the crime, leave out "en": "Han blev anklaget for bestikkelse" (He was accused of bribery).

besvær.explanation: "Et besvær" means "a hassle". To answer someone who thanks you for your effort: "Tak for hjælpen." "Det er ikke noget besvær." (Thanks for the help. It is no trouble.)

besværlig.explanation: "Besværlig" means "troublesome". It comes from "et besvær" (a hassle). When you talk about a person who is awkward to deal with, use it too: "en besværlig kunde" (a difficult customer).

beton.explanation: "Beton" means "concrete". When you mean the material in general, leave out "en": "Der er beton overalt" (There is concrete everywhere). Do not mix it up with "cement" (cement), the powder: "Cement er et gråt pulver" (Cement is a gray powder).
